## THE CENTRAL STRUCTURAL MOVE

The shipped surface is seven stacked blocks (header, regen band, 4-tile grid, three full-width shop rows, footer). This rebuild is FOUR grid rows, each sharing its zones on one row per RULINGS law 8's closing lesson ('a row you do not share is a row you pay for in full'): (1) a TOP STRIP pairing the demoted day marker with the strain readout, (2) a PICK ROW pairing the focal hero card with a compact strip of the other options, (3) a SHOP ROW putting all three purchases three-up instead of stacked, (4) a FOOTER row (unchanged shape). Total distinct text/readout tokens across the surface is roughly 25 to 27, against LOADOUT's much larger census: this panel is meant to prove the system holds at low density, and per the brief it is expected to land well under the 700px target, not just under the 820px ceiling. My own row-height estimate (title ~36 + body padding ~24 + top strip ~80 + pick row ~195 + shop row ~170 + footer ~55 + 3 gaps ~33) totals roughly 590px; that is a build target to aim for and sanity-check against, not a substitute for the Orchestrator's own CDP measurement.

## GLANCE ORDER (law 2)

1ST, FOCAL: THE PICK (the hero card inside the pick row). It is the only thing on the surface the player must ACT on, it is permanent for the rest of the run once closed, and it is the thing blocking the exit (CLOSE THE NIGHT). Law 2 demands one focal element at extreme scale enforcing a stated order; making the pick focal is the only reading under which the type scale is doing real work, because it is the only candidate that is a DECISION rather than a readout.

2ND: STRAIN (the top-strip strain readout). It is the run's life and the number the night's purchases exist to defend, so it earns real prominence and keeps its full three-channel alarm treatment in the risk band, but it is a READOUT the player nudges indirectly (by buying a patch) rather than a choice resolved on this screen. Giving it focal scale would also put a second loud element right beside the one channel (--r-warn) that law 1 requires to stay rare to keep working. Demoted to 2nd priority: still legible at a real (not tiny) scale, sharing the top row.

REJECTED CANDIDATE, DAY NUMERAL: demoted to an ambient masthead slab sharing the top-strip row with strain, at roughly a third of the hero's scale. Reason for rejection: it is 'pure state with no decision attached' (the brief's own framing) -- a chapter marker the player reads once per night and moves past, not a choice they must resolve before the window's exit unlocks. It takes NO role token (not --r-data, which the role assignment below reserves for the focal numeral only); it renders in plain ambient ink, exactly like an ordinary readout line, signalling its demotion by treatment as well as by size.

AMBIENT: the shop row's three cells (ghost buttons, status lines, pip/rack rows) and the footer's pointer line. All plain --r-struct chrome and dim text, never competing for first read.

## TYPE SCALE (enforcing the order)

All tokens declared once on the outer .nt-grid container (container-type: inline-size; container-name: nt on the wrapping .nt-eva), all clamp() on cqi, all resolving AT THE USE SITE per the documented loadout-eva gotcha (a token used inside a narrower nested container lands smaller than the same token used at the window's own width):

- --nt-fs-body: clamp(19px, calc(1cqi + 17px), 21px) -- VT323 body floor, identical ratio to loadout's --lo-fs-body.
- --nt-fs-label: clamp(9px, calc(0.6cqi + 8px), 11px) -- Silkscreen annotation floor, identical to loadout's --lo-fs-label.
- --nt-fs-pill: clamp(10px, calc(0.6cqi + 9px), 12px) -- strip-row and shop-cell button labels, one step above the label floor.
- --nt-fs-slab: clamp(18px, 2.4cqi, 24px) -- the demoted DAY N CLOSED marker.
- --nt-fs-strain: clamp(22px, 3.2cqi, 30px) -- the strain value, resolved against the FULL window container (the top strip spans both grid columns).
- --nt-fs-hero: clamp(48px, 12.5cqi, 82px) -- THE FOCAL TOKEN. Declared on .nt-grid like every other token, but only ever USED inside .nt-hero (the hero card), which must itself be container-type: inline-size; container-name: nthero, so this cqi ramp resolves against the hero card's own width (roughly 58% of window content, ~416 to 521px across the three supported viewports) rather than the window's full width. This is deliberate and mirrors loadout's own --lo-fs-body behaviour; state it in a build comment so nobody treats the smaller-than-window-cqi result as a bug.

Ratio proof (law 2 requires >=2x, ideally more): computed at each supported viewport's WIDE-tier content box (16:9 window 860px -> content ~826px, hero card ~474px; 21:9 window 940px -> content ~906px, hero card ~521px; laptop window 760px -> content ~726px, hero card ~416px), --nt-fs-hero evaluates to roughly 59px / 65px / 52px respectively (all within the clamp's floor-to-peak range, none clipped), while --nt-fs-strain (resolved against the full content width at the same three viewports) evaluates to roughly 26px / 29px / 23px. Ratios: 2.23x / 2.24x / 2.24x. Consistently over 2x at all three supported viewports; this is the number the Orchestrator should re-derive and hold as an acceptance target once real padding/gap values are in place, not treat as exact.

The hero glyph itself must never be a long label string (VT323/Silkscreen at 48-82px cannot hold a 19-character name on one line without overflowing a ~450px card) -- see PICK ZONE COMPOSITION below for the exact per-tile split that keeps the hero token to 2-7 characters.

## NAMED ZONES

### Z1 TOP STRIP (shares one row; masthead left, strain right)
Glyph budget: ~7-8 tokens. Left cluster (.nt-mast-l): an eyebrow 'NIGHT.SYS // DAY CLOSE' (--r-note, structural label matching loadout's own eyebrow idiom, not narrative copy) and, at --nt-fs-slab, 'DAY {n} CLOSED' (plain ambient ink, no role -- see glance order above) built from the shipped Hero-numeral usage's own text ('DAY' + the day number + 'CLOSED'), plus ONE retained sentence from the shipped header paragraph, verbatim: 'One upgrade holds for the rest of the run.' (see CUTS for why the other two sentences are dropped), at --nt-fs-body, dim ambient ink.
Right cluster (.nt-strainzone): label 'STRAIN' (--r-note) over a 30-segment meter (SegMeter equivalent, segs=30, matching the shipped <SegMeter segs={30}/> exactly) plus a value readout at --nt-fs-strain and, conditionally, the '+{lastRegen} STRAIN' pop. Colour banding: NOMINAL (>70) = --r-ok on both meter fill and number; NEUTRAL (36-70) = --r-line on both; RISK (<=35) = --r-warn on both PLUS the composited alarm (see ALARM below). Unfilled segments and the meter's outer track are --r-struct in every band. The '+N STRAIN' pop is always --r-ok regardless of the settling band, because a gain is good news even mid-alarm.

### Z2 PICK ROW (shares one row; hero card left ~58%, strip right ~38%, ~12-14px gap)
Glyph budget: ~8-9 tokens (1 pname + 1 hero token + 1 detail sentence + 1 SELECTED stamp, plus up to 4 strip-row labels). This is the surface's densest zone and its focal panel.

Hero card (.nt-hero, container-type inline-size): 1px --r-struct hairline border (base panel edge) PLUS 24px length / 4px --r-hazard heavy corner brackets (law 4's exact stated dimensions, reused verbatim from loadout's .lo-bracket, scoped to this ONE focal panel only -- no other panel on the surface gets heavy brackets). Contents, top to bottom: pname caption at --nt-fs-label / --r-note (the tile's system name, e.g. 'SCAN.EXE', or 'RAM / TURN' for the ram pick); the hero glyph at --nt-fs-hero / --r-data (THE ONLY use of --r-data on the surface); a detail line at --nt-fs-body, plain ambient ink, the tile's own shipped sentence verbatim; a 'SELECTED' stamp (shipped word, small caps chip) at --r-ok, shown only when a real pick is active. When a pick IS active, an INNER 8px length / 2px --r-ok corner-tick reticle (law 6's house idiom, reused verbatim from loadout's .lo-mode.mode-on::before/::after) appears inset roughly 6-8px from the outer hazard brackets, so the two nested corner treatments never collide: the outer 24px/4px hazard brackets say 'this is the focal panel' (always present), the inner 8px/2px ok reticle says 'this option is selected' (present only post-pick).

Pre-pick ('NO PICK') state: the hero card renders at the IDENTICAL footprint and the IDENTICAL --nt-fs-hero type size, showing the status word 'NO PICK' (minted to match the existing SELECTED/MAXED all-caps status-word family; flagged honestly here as a new word rather than hidden, since it is one syllable beyond a bare noun -- swap for a copy-ordered word for free if the reviewer wants one) in dashed --r-struct chrome, --ch-faint ink, no detail line, no stamp, no inner reticle (only the outer hazard brackets, since it is still the focal panel by position even with nothing selected). Since NightPick is always null on a fresh mount (the reducer's resultNext case always sets nightPick: null when entering the upgrade screen), every one of the four RUN STATE variations LOADS into this NO PICK state; picking is a live demo interaction, not baked into the initial render.

PICK ZONE COMPOSITION (the exact hero/pname split per tile, verbatim substrings of the shipped labels, never reworded): 
- ram, live label '+1 RAM / TURN' -> hero token '+1' (characters before the first space), pname 'RAM / TURN' (the remainder). Detail: '{ramPerTurn} to {ramPerTurn+1}. More moves, more programs, every single turn.' verbatim per state.
- scan, live label 'SCAN.EXE T{n} > T{n+1}' -> pname 'SCAN.EXE' (before the first space), hero token 'T{n} > T{n+1}' (the remainder, e.g. 'T2 > T3', 7 characters, comfortably short at hero scale). Detail (static regardless of tier, shipped verbatim): 'Wider sweep radius. Still always 1 RAM.'
- attack, live label 'ATTACK.EXE T{n} > T{n+1}' -> pname 'ATTACK.EXE', hero 'T{n} > T{n+1}'. Detail (static, verbatim): 'One more node per cast: redirect or trap in bulk.'
- defend, live label 'DEFEND.EXE T{n} > T{n+1}' -> pname 'DEFEND.EXE', hero 'T{n} > T{n+1}'. Detail (static, verbatim): 'One more node per cast: purge, lock, or a wider ward.'
Note the split direction inverts between ram (hero = the token BEFORE the first space) and the three .exe tiles (hero = the token AFTER the first space); this is a fixed 4-row table, not a general algorithm, and should be hardcoded as such rather than derived at runtime by string-splitting heuristics.

Strip (.nt-strip, flex column, 3 rows post-pick or up to 4 pre-pick): each row shows the tile's FULL shipped label as one string at --nt-fs-pill, no split, no detail line (see CUTS for why maxed detail sentences never surface, and why live detail sentences are safe to omit here). Live rows are plain ink, clickable, 2px --r-struct border; MAXED rows show the shipped 'X MAXED' string verbatim in dashed 2px --r-struct border, --ch-faint ink, non-interactive (aria-disabled, no pointer events). No corner-tick reticle in the strip -- reticles mark ONLY the actual selected state, which by construction can only live in the hero slot.

Interaction: clicking any live strip row promotes it into the hero slot (replacing whatever was there) and demotes the previous hero content back into the strip as a new row; this does double duty as BOTH 'select' and 'preview the detail sentence', which is sound specifically because the pick is free and fully reversible until CLOSE THE NIGHT -- unlike LOADOUT's paid boost bays, no separate hover/tap popup layer is needed here (see UN-ADDED). Transition: the hero card's inner content cross-fades via the shared kp-slot-in keyframe (300ms, steps(5), translateY+opacity, reused verbatim, no new keyframe) whenever the pick changes, including the very first resolve on load; the demoted strip row plays a brief highlight flash (2px --r-struct border brightening to full --ch for one steps(2) cycle, ~140ms) so the eye can follow where it landed. sfx: shipped 'tick' fires on every click that changes the pick (mirrors the shipped chooseUpgrade dispatch exactly).

PICK STATE MACHINE, the three guarantees law 6 demands unmissable: (a) EXACTLY ONE selected -- enforced structurally, not just by styling: there is exactly one hero slot in the DOM and the strip is derived as 'every other live/maxed option', so the layout cannot represent two simultaneous selections even by a styling mistake. (b) REVERSIBLE until CLOSE THE NIGHT -- demonstrated live: clicking strip option A then B swaps A back into the strip and B into the hero with no confirmation, no cost, no lock, matching the shipped chooseUpgrade case exactly (it does not end the night). (c) CLOSE THE NIGHT locked until a pick exists -- the button is disabled/inert while the internal pick state is null (mirrors the shipped closeNight guard run.nightPick === null) and becomes enabled plus armed (--r-ok fill, matching the role assignment's explicit 'armed state of CLOSE THE NIGHT') the instant any live strip row is clicked; the footer pointer line swaps in lockstep between the shipped 'Pick one upgrade above to close the night.' and 'Closing the night applies {NIGHT_PICK_LABEL[pick]} and opens day {day+1}.' (NIGHT_PICK_LABEL transcribed verbatim: ram -> '+1 RAM / TURN', scan -> 'the SCAN.EXE tier', attack -> 'the ATTACK.EXE tier', defend -> 'the DEFEND.EXE tier'). For DAY 9 CAPPED, once ram is picked this correctly reads '...and opens day 10.' -- the shipped template has no separate finale-specific wording (FINAL_DAY=10 is the ordinary day+1 arithmetic, nothing more), so none is invented here.

### Z3 SHOP ROW (shares one row; three cells, roughly equal width, e.g. 1fr 1.15fr 1fr favouring the pouch cell's glyph row)
Glyph budget: ~8 tokens (3 button labels + 3 status sentences + 1 pip row + 1 glyph rack). Each cell (.nt-shop-cell) is a plain hairline --r-struct bordered box (the .lo-sub SHELL reused, its subhead+chip header treatment dropped -- see UN-ADDED): a ghost button carrying the shipped label verbatim, then the shipped status sentence verbatim at --nt-fs-body in plain dim ambient ink (no per-token colour splitting -- see UN-ADDED), then whatever auxiliary readout the row needs.

- Cell 1, NIGHT PATCH: button label 'NIGHT PATCH: +{PATCH_HEAL} STRAIN ({nightPatchCost(day)} cr)' (PATCH_HEAL=12 constant); status 'STRAIN {strain}/100 - {credits} cr - rest restored +{DAY_REST_REGEN}' (DAY_REST_REGEN=10 is a FLAT constant describing the rule, not this session's lastRegen -- DAY 2 EARLY and DAY 9 CAPPED both correctly read 'rest restored +10' even though their own lastRegen is 0, because the sentence describes what resting always does, not what it just did; transcribe this exactly, it is shipped behaviour, not a bug to fix). Disabled (--r-struct dashed, not --r-warn) when credits < cost OR strain >= 100, matching the shipped guard exactly.
- Cell 2, BUY BLIND: button label 'BUY BLIND: SEE DARKNET.LNK', status 'POUCH {pouch.length}/{PATCH_POUCH_MAX} - {credits} cr - Pay first. Shape is the surprise.' (PATCH_POUCH_MAX=5), plus the pouch RACK reused verbatim from loadout-eva's .lo-rack: each held piece as a PatchGlyph (reused unmodified from kp.css, no new colour treatment) plus its shape noun label at --nt-fs-label/--r-note (per the role assignment's explicit 'pouch shape nouns' owner), and a dashed --r-struct .lo-hole placeholder for each remaining slot up to 5, so a 1-piece pouch and a 5-piece pouch occupy the SAME rack footprint. This button carries NO disabled state in the shipped source (affordability and pouch-full guards live inside DARKNET.LNK, out of scope here) -- it is always live. In this standalone study, where no DARKNET.LNK window exists to open, clicking it is INERT: no sound (the shipped source calls no sfx on this control either) and no visible change, explicitly not a placeholder bug.
- Cell 3, INSTALL BOOST BAY: button label 'INSTALL BOOST BAY ({slotCost} cr)' or '(MAX)' when slotCost is null (BOOST_SLOTS_MAX=5 reached); status 'BAYS {augments.length}/{boostSlots} - {credits} cr' (numerator is bays OCCUPIED by held augments, denominator is CAPACITY purchased -- these are different numbers, both must be tracked per run state); a PipRow reused verbatim (filled={boostSlots}, total=BOOST_SLOTS_MAX=5, matching the shipped <PipRow filled={run.boostSlots}.../> exactly -- filled tracks CAPACITY bought, not augments held); the shipped pointer sentence verbatim, 'A full bay drafts as a swap. More bays, more boosts held.' Disabled (--r-struct) when slotCost is null or credits < slotCost.

A hazard-stripe divider (law 4, --r-hazard, 45deg, reused verbatim from loadout's .lo-div) sits above this row with the structural label 'NIGHT SHOP' (--ch-dim, matching loadout's own '// BENCH SUPPORT' divider-label precedent -- structural chrome, not narrative copy).

Interactions stay LIVE per the brief (unlike loadout-eva, which left DIVE and the pouch inert as a pure study): buyPatch (enabled) deducts nightPatchCost(day) credits and adds PATCH_HEAL=12 strain clamped to 100, replaying the SAME 150ms-delay-free version of the strain-fill mechanism used at load (see LOAD CHOREOGRAPHY: 0ms lead instead of 150ms, since this is a direct click response not a page reveal), firing sfx 'granted' (NOT dayCloseRegen, which is reserved for the mount-time rest event per the shipped code's own separate sfx('granted') call on buyPatch) and, if the result crosses a band threshold, the strain readout's band class and alarm state re-evaluate live at fill-completion. buySlot (enabled) deducts slotCost credits, increments boostSlots, lights one more pip via kp-slot-in, and updates cell 3's own button cost/label and status line; it does NOT change augments.length. Both purchase buttons fire sfx 'granted' on success, matching shipped code exactly; both remain silently inert when disabled (no deny sfx exists in the shipped set for this surface, so none is added).

### Z4 FOOTER (single row, unchanged shape from shipped)
Glyph budget: 2 tokens. Pointer line (plain ambient ink, dynamic per PICK STATE MACHINE above) and the CLOSE THE NIGHT button (--r-ok fill when armed, --r-struct dashed disabled outline when not, matching the role assignment's explicit ownership). sfx: shipped 'dayClose' fires on click (only reachable when armed).

## FLUID RULES

Container: .nt-eva { container-type: inline-size; container-name: nt; } wraps the window body content; .nt-hero additionally establishes its OWN nested container (container-name: nthero) so --nt-fs-hero resolves against the card's width, not the window's. One binary breakpoint at 700px of content inline-size (RULINGS law 3), identical threshold to loadout-eva. Window (.term) widths per viewport, reused identical to loadout-eva for tiling consistency and because this panel's own column structure (2-col pick row, 3-col shop row) needs comparable room: 16:9 -> 860px, 21:9 -> 940px, laptop 1280x800 -> 760px; content boxes roughly window-34px, comfortably clearing 700px at all three (laptop's 726px matches loadout's own proven-safe figure).

WIDE tier (>=700px, all three supported viewports): grid-template-columns: minmax(0,1.4fr) minmax(0,1fr); grid-template-areas: 'top top' / 'hero strip' / 'shop shop' / 'foot foot'.

NARROW tier (<700px, a tiling fallback only -- no supported viewport reaches it, per RULINGS law 3): single column, grid-template-areas: 'top' / 'hero' / 'strip' / 'shop' / 'foot'; the strip reflows from a vertical stack into a horizontal row of compact chips (flex-wrap) to spend the now-full-width, now-precious-height differently; the shop row's three cells stack to one column. No scrollbar in either tier, ever.

## LOAD CHOREOGRAPHY

All timings below are the demo's target values; REDUCED reduces every later(fn, delay) call to fn() at delay 0 (the shipped later() helper, reused verbatim), so every element in this list appears in its FINAL state on the first frame, sound unaffected (law 7).

- t=0ms: static chrome (borders, brackets, divider, labels) renders instantly, no animation -- ambient chrome never animates, on load or after. The strain meter and number render at the PRE-rest value (run.strain - run.lastRegen, or run.strain unchanged if lastRegen<=0) instantly, no motion, matching the shipped strainShown logic exactly.
- t=150ms (exact, per the brief and the shipped setTimeout): IF lastRegen>0, sfx 'dayCloseRegen' fires (ui bus) AND the strain meter begins a 300ms, steps(8) transition from the pre-rest fill percentage to the post-rest fill percentage -- reusing the shipped SegMeter's own stated parameters (dur=300, steps=8) rather than inventing a new cadence. The number synchronises: an 8-tick count from pre-rest to post-rest across the same 300ms window.
- t=450ms: fill complete. The '+{lastRegen} STRAIN' pop appears via the shared kp-slot-in keyframe (300ms, steps(5), reused verbatim).
- SILENT BRANCH (lastRegen===0, exercised by DAY 2 EARLY and DAY 9 CAPPED): none of the above fires. No sfx, no segment motion, no pop. The meter simply sits at its already-full value from t=0, matching law 4's equal-footprint spirit applied to TIME as well as space -- a 'nothing happens' branch that still occupies the identical layout and timing slot, just silently.
- t=220ms: the hero card's NO PICK placeholder content steps in (kp-slot-in, reused, 300ms).
- t=300/390/480/570ms (90ms stagger): the strip's up to 4 rows slot in one by one (kp-slot-in), matching loadout's own bay/pouch stagger cadence.
- t=700/800/900ms (100ms stagger): the shop row's 3 cells slot in (kp-slot-in); within the pouch cell, held-piece glyphs stagger a further 70ms apart starting 60ms after their cell's own reveal. The pip row in cell 3 fills statically with its cell -- no extra choreography (see UN-ADDED, not every readout needs its own animation).
- t=1050ms: the footer fades in (opacity 0->1, 120ms, steps(3)).
- Total settle: roughly 1.2s to the footer's arrival, deliberately shorter than loadout-eva's ~2.1 to 2.5s full sweep -- proportionate to this surface's own lower density, not a compressed copy of loadout's timeline.
- REPLAY LOAD (a rig button, not a real multi-option switch -- see VARIATIONS) clears all pending timers and animation classes (the shipped clearTimers()/sweep() pattern, reused verbatim) and re-runs this entire sequence against the CURRENTLY selected run state, including a fresh regen fill if that state's lastRegen>0; it does not re-roll or change any value.
- Manual buyPatch purchases reuse the SAME 300ms/steps(8) fill routine with 0ms lead delay (a direct click response, not a page reveal) and sfx 'granted' in place of 'dayCloseRegen'; this is a build-economy note (one fill function, two call sites: mount timer and click handler), not a second animation to design.
- No LOADING -> READY slab transition (unlike loadout-eva's masthead): NIGHT.SYS has no analogous 'not yet resolved' state for the day marker to transition out of, so borrowing that flourish would be decorative mimicry rather than a real state change (see UN-ADDED).

## ROLE ASSIGNMENT (all eight tokens, every one an explicit owner or an explicit non-owner)

- --r-struct: chrome and borders throughout -- every panel/card hairline, the meter track and unfilled segments, unfilled pips, dashed disabled outlines (MAXED strip rows, the NO PICK placeholder, disabled shop buttons at cap or short credits). Matches the role table's own literal wording ('disabled outlines').
- --r-note: naming labels only, never values -- the masthead eyebrow, 'STRAIN', the hero card's pname caption (system name or unit tag), the shop row's cell/zone labels, the pouch's shape-noun text (Elbow/Tee/etc, per the brief's explicit instruction), and the 'cr' suffix specifically inside button cost labels (e.g. the 'cr' in 'INSTALL BOOST BAY (150 cr)' is styled apart from the '150' -- scoped to button labels only, NOT to the freeform status sentences, which stay plain ambient per UN-ADDED).
- --r-line: live values and filled slots -- the strain meter/number in the NEUTRAL band (36-70), filled boost-bay pips, patch-glyph arms (reused unmodified from kp.css), and the numeral portion of cost figures inside button labels (the '150' in '150 cr').
- --r-data: THE FOCAL NUMERAL ONLY. Its single use on this surface is the hero glyph inside the pick card (the '+1' or 'T2 > T3' token). Not the strain number, not the day marker, not any cost figure -- reserved exactly as the brief instructs ('--r-data owns the focal numeral only').
- --r-ok: NOMINAL and selected/armed states -- the SELECTED stamp, the hero card's inner corner-tick reticle when a pick is active, the strain readout in the NOMINAL band (>70), the '+N STRAIN' pop (always, regardless of settling band), and CLOSE THE NIGHT's armed fill.
- --r-warn: RISK, and nothing else, ever. Its only appearance on this surface is the strain readout (number AND meter fill together, treated as one composite readout) when strain<=35, carrying the full three-channel alarm (see ALARM below). Explicitly NOT used on MAXED tiles, NOT on 'cannot afford' shop states, NOT on the empty pouch/bay pips -- all of those take --r-struct instead, so nobody reaches for red twice.
- --r-aux: UNOWNED on this surface, explicitly, because the IMAGERY decision below is NO IMAGERY -- there is no camera or feed for this token to tint.
- --r-hazard: structural red -- the window's outer .term border (matching every other panel), the pick card's heavy 24px/4px corner brackets (the surface's one focal panel), and the hazard-stripe divider above the shop row.

## ALARM (law 1's three channels)

Thresholds reused unchanged from loadout-eva per the brief's instruction ('reuse them unless there is a reason not to'; no reason found): NOMINAL above 70 (--r-ok), NEUTRAL between 36 and 70 (--r-line), RISK at or below 35 (--r-warn). Note the polarity: strain counts DOWN as the run wears, so the risk band is the LOW end of the meter, the inverse of a typical 'fuller is worse' read -- both the meter fill and the number itself flip to --r-warn together (a composite readout, not two separately-triggered pieces) when strain<=35.

Three channels, composited exactly per loadout-eva's measured, cheaper mechanism (never animate background/box-shadow inside the CRT-glassed subtree -- measured there at 50ms p95 versus 9.3ms p95 for the compositor-only version): (1) COLOUR -- the readout's own --r-warn fill, a hotter, purer red distinct from the ambient --r-hazard tone, so risk never shares its colour with the surface's structural chrome. (2) INVERSE VIDEO -- the readout's base (non-animated) styling floods to a solid --r-warn block with void/--px-void digits, which is the constant state under the alarm, always present, not itself animated. (3) MOTION -- a difference-blend plate (position:absolute, inset -2px over the readout, background:var(--r-warn), mix-blend-mode:difference, opacity:0, will-change:opacity), reused verbatim from loadout's .lo-riskflash, animating opacity 0<->1 on the shipped 1.2s steps(2) cadence (kp-danger-blink's own cadence). Ambient chrome (window border, corner brackets, divider) NEVER animates, which is the entire mechanism: five-plus static red shapes elsewhere train the eye to stop sampling red, so motion is the one channel only the alarm has. Under reduced motion the plate's animation is removed (opacity forced to 0) and the alarm falls back to the static inverse flood alone, still colourblind-legible, mirroring loadout's own reduced-motion fallback exactly.

## IMAGERY DECISION: NO IMAGERY

--r-aux stays unowned and no FEED variation exists. Argued per the brief's own framing: (1) this surface's job is a decision plus a status readout plus a small shop, none of which has a DISTINCT diegetic camera moment the way LOADOUT.CFG's 'operator rig' does (that surface is literally about watching the bench while configuring the kit; NIGHT.SYS is not). (2) The only candidate raw asset (_shared/art/raw/raw-solder-bench.png) is the SAME bench camera LOADOUT.CFG already owns; reusing it here is decorative duplication across two windows in the same desktop, not a new diegetic beat, and law 5 requires an in-fiction REASON, not just an available file. (3) This panel's whole job is proving the system holds at low density (law 11); the height budget above is already fully earned by the pick, strain and shop content, and adding an imagery cell would either steal width from the focal pick row or get cropped into an unreadable sliver -- law 8 step 1 says cut outright rather than force imagery that cannot survive its size, so it is cut outright here rather than added and then cut.

## CUTS TAKEN (law 8, recorded)

1. The shipped header's three-sentence paragraph is cut to its first sentence only, verbatim ('One upgrade holds for the rest of the run.'); the other two sentences (sequencing and reversibility) now read off the pick state machine itself (demote-on-click, the disabled-until-picked CLOSE button) plus the unchanged footer pointer line, which already carries the scheduling information. Law 8 step 2: a paragraph reduced to a pointer sentence once its explanation is owned elsewhere -- here 'elsewhere' is this surface's own new interactive structure, not a different window.
2. The four tiles' MAXED-state detail sentences (ram's distinct 'Already at the per turn cap of {MAX_RAM}.', and the scan/attack/defend sentences, which the shipped source actually leaves unchanged even once maxed) never surface: a maxed option can never occupy the hero slot by construction, so the promote-to-reveal mechanism can never reach them, and the MAXED stamp plus dashed chrome already state the fact. This quietly avoids a mildly confusing shipped-copy quirk (scan/attack/defend's detail text still reads like upgrade advice even after that tree is capped) without rewording anything -- it is simply never displayed.
3. Imagery cut outright (see IMAGERY DECISION).
4. The shipped grid's four co-equal tiles become one hero plus a three-item strip, and the three shipped full-width shop rows become one three-up row: neither is a content loss (every tile's full content still exists, promoted or compact; every shop control keeps its exact shipped label and status sentence), it is a SHAPE change that answers law 8's closing lesson directly.

## DELIBERATELY UN-ADDED (unusual for this panel, and requested explicitly)

1. No masthead CREDITS summary chip, despite loadout-eva precedent and its cheapness: credits already appear inline in every shop row's shipped status sentence and cost label; a duplicate chip is decoration this low-density panel does not need, and the brief's whole warning here is against inventing filler.
2. No hover/tap popup layer for strip rows (unlike loadout's paid boost-bay popups): clicking a strip row is free, reversible and instant, so 'preview' and 'select' collapse into one action; a popup layer would be solving a problem (irreversible or costly preview) this surface does not have.
3. No imagery cell (see IMAGERY DECISION).
4. No per-token colour-splitting inside the three shop row's freeform status sentences (the STRAIN/POUCH/BAYS lines) -- left as plain ambient dim text; the shop row is deliberately ambient-priority already, and investing typographic hierarchy inside it would fight the surface's own extreme-contrast goal rather than serve it.
5. No additional strain sub-band beyond nominal/neutral/risk (e.g. no separate 'critical' near zero): the brief's stated thresholds are reused unchanged, no reason found to add a fourth band.
6. No confirmation modal on CLOSE THE NIGHT: the shipped anatomy has none, and the surface's own message is already 'nothing is locked in until you press it' -- a second confirmation step would contradict that, not reinforce it.
7. Only one hazard-stripe divider (above the shop row), not a second one between the top strip and the pick row: a second divider would compete with the pick card's own corner brackets for 'this is a boundary' attention without marking a boundary the reader actually needs (the size jump into the hero glyph already reads as a zone change).
8. No LOADING -> READY slab transition on the day marker (see LOAD CHOREOGRAPHY): there is no shipped 'not yet resolved' state for NIGHT.SYS's day counter to transition out of, unlike loadout's kit-readiness slab.

## GATE-SHAPED CONCERN (not escalated, recorded here per the brief)

See the gateNote field.

## SOUND

All four shipped presets reused verbatim, no new sfx items proposed: 'tick' (ui bus) on every pick-changing strip click; 'dayCloseRegen' (ui bus) at t=150ms on mount only when lastRegen>0; 'granted' (ui bus) on every successful buyPatch or buySlot dispatch, INCLUDING the manual mid-session patch purchase (which reuses the fill visuals but not the dayCloseRegen sound, since that preset is reserved for the mount-time rest event in the shipped source); 'dayClose' (ui bus) on CLOSE THE NIGHT. BUY BLIND has no sfx in the shipped source and gets none here.

items.gateNote: Pure UI cycle per RULINGS.md 'Process': no loremaster or tutorial gate ran this cycle. One gate-shaped residue for the eventual integration pass: the two teaching moments mounted on this surface, day-upgrade (content/teaching.ts, anchor 'grid', order 70) and night-shop (anchor 'patch', order 71), currently position via fixed-pixel offsets measured against the SHIPPED layout (kp-teach-grid: top 150px/left 30px; kp-teach-patch: top 56px/right 24px, styles.css). This spec's PICK ROW is the direct successor to the old .kp-upgrade-grid (day-upgrade's natural anchor) and the shop row's first cell (NIGHT PATCH) is the direct successor to the old first .kp-patchrow (night-shop's natural anchor); both landing spots exist and are reachable in the new layout, so the anchors are not orphaned. But the fixed-pixel coordinates will need retargeting at integration, and since this layout is fluid (cqi-based) rather than fixed, switching these two anchors to a relative/cqi-based offset at the same time is worth doing rather than re-guessing new fixed pixels against a layout that itself scales. Flagged for the Orchestrator's integration pass, not solved in this pure-UI study, and not treated as a loremaster/tutorial gate question since nothing about WHAT is taught changes, only where the callout points.

In DAY 8 STRAINED, the strain readout's computed background/text colour differs from its NOMINAL and NEUTRAL band colours (channel 1: colour); the readout's base styling is a solid inverse-flooded block, void text on --r-warn, present independent of any animation state (channel 2: inverse video); a difference-blend plate over the readout oscillates opacity between 0 and 1 on a ~1.2s cycle, sampled at two points within one cycle to confirm motion (channel 3: motion); the window border, the pick card's corner brackets, and the shop-row divider show animation-name: none / no computed-style change across the same sampling window (ambient chrome stays static)
